learningObjectives: Differentiate UI design from UX design and explain how they work together.
Identify the core stages of a human-centered design process.
Recognize usability, accessibility, and user needs as key design considerations.

activities.title: UI vs UX Explorer
activities.instruction: Choose whether each responsibility is primarily UI or UX.

content.concept: UI focuses on the interface's visual and interactive elements, while UX focuses on the broader experience, user goals, workflows, and problem-solving.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

choices: UI: Designing colors, typography, spacing, and visual components
UX: Researching user needs and improving task flows
config.answer: UI: Designing colors, typography, spacing, and visual components

activities.title: Human-Centered Design Map
activities.instruction: Explore the stages of a human-centered design process.

content.concept: Human-centered design starts with understanding people and their context, then moves through defining problems, exploring solutions, prototyping, testing, and iterating.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

descriptions: Understand users, their context, behaviors, goals, and pain points.
Synthesize research into a clear problem statement or design challenge.
Generate multiple possible solutions before choosing a direction.
Create a simple representation of a solution that users can interact with.
Evaluate the design with users, learn from feedback, and improve the solution.

activities.title: Usability Check
activities.instruction: Choose the interface that makes the task easier to complete.

content.concept: Usability describes how effectively, efficiently, and easily users can accomplish their goals. Clear navigation, readable content, and understandable controls reduce unnecessary effort.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

choices: Clear labels, readable text, visible actions, and simple navigation
Unclear icons, tiny text, hidden actions, and confusing navigation
config.answer: Clear labels, readable text, visible actions, and simple navigation

activities.title: UX Principle Explorer
activities.instruction: Explore examples of important UX principles.

content.concept: Consistency, feedback, visibility, simplicity, and user control help users understand what is happening and predict how an interface will behave.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

descriptions: Use similar patterns and controls consistently across the interface.
Show users the result or status of their actions, such as a success message or loading indicator.
Make important information, system status, and available actions easy to discover.
Remove unnecessary complexity so users can focus on their goals.
Allow users to undo, cancel, go back, or otherwise control their actions when appropriate.
